general.lead: RailSafe AI is a desktop monitoring system for railway crossings using cameras, AI detection and PLC signals.

blocks.title: In simple words
items: The dashboard shows each crossing as a card with live video, vehicle counts, train status and statistics.
AI detects light and heavy vehicles from the camera image.
If PLC is connected, train approach is shown as a separate safety state.

blocks.title: What is on the main screen?
items: Top toolbar: Dashboard, Add Crossing, Refresh, Settings, Analytics and About.
Crossing card: video, daily vehicle count, train count and PLC state.
Analytics page: daily, weekly and monthly charts plus Word reports.

blocks.title: Operator rule
blocks.text: Add the crossing first, connect the camera, then check polygon and PLC settings. After that the system monitors automatically.

start.lead: An operator who receives the EXE can start with this sequence.

blocks.title: Minimum launch path
items: Open RailSafe.exe and wait for the main window.
On first launch the AI model may prepare for 10-30 seconds; this is normal.
Click + Add Crossing and enter the crossing name and location.
Open the crossing card and add at least one main camera.
Enter the RTSP URL or choose a video file for testing.
Select a polygon file if available, or leave it empty and add it later.
If PLC exists, enter IP and port; otherwise keep PLC disabled for now.
Return to dashboard and check camera status, occupancy and vehicle count.

blocks.title: Be patient on first launch
blocks.text: While the AI model, camera stream or TensorRT engine is preparing, video may be hidden for a while. If the app looks busy, wait 1-2 minutes first.

blocks.title: Ready-to-work checklist
items: Camera is not stuck on Connecting and video is visible.
Light/Heavy/Total numbers change when vehicles pass.
If polygon exists, Occupancy becomes greater than 0 when a vehicle enters the zone.
If PLC is connected, PLC state shows Connected or Train approaching.

crossing.lead: A crossing is one railway crossing monitored by the system. Each crossing has its own cameras, PLC settings and statistics.

blocks.title: Add a crossing
items: Click + Add Crossing on the top toolbar.
Enter a short clear name, for example Crossing 8.
Enter the object location.
Add an optional description if needed.
If PLC is ready, enable it on the PLC Settings tab; otherwise keep it disabled.
Click Save. The crossing appears as a card on the dashboard.

blocks.title: When to add multiple crossings?
blocks.text: If you monitor several real railway crossings or independent checkpoints, add each one as a separate crossing.

blocks.title: Be careful before deleting
blocks.text: Deleting a crossing can remove its camera settings and statistics. Export reports or JSON backup first.

camera.lead: A camera is needed to see the crossing and count vehicles. At least one main camera is recommended.

blocks.title: Add a camera
items: Open the crossing card.
Click + Camera.
Give the camera a name, for example A1 or North direction.
Choose Main or Additional. Main camera is shown in the large view.
Enter the RTSP URL or video file path.
Check that Enable camera and Enable detection are selected.
Click Save and wait for video.

blocks.title: RTSP examples
items: Common format: rtsp://login:password@IP:554/channel
Common Hikvision format: rtsp://admin:password@192.168.1.50:554/Streaming/Channels/101
If it does not open, test the same RTSP URL in VLC Media Player.

blocks.title: Main camera rule
blocks.text: One crossing should have one main camera. Extra cameras are used as additional views or replace the current main camera.

plc.lead: PLC tells the system that a train is approaching. It is shown together with camera occupancy for safety awareness.

blocks.title: Connect PLC
items: Open Add/Edit Crossing and go to PLC Settings.
Enable PLC.
Enter IP address, for example 192.168.170.159.
Port is usually 102 unless your automation specialist gives another value.
Test connection if the button is available, then save.

blocks.title: PLC states
items: CONNECTED - communication works and the system waits for train signal.
TRAIN APPROACHING - PLC active signal is received; operator should watch the crossing zone.
NO CONNECTION - check IP, cable, network or PLC settings.
DISABLED - PLC monitoring is not used for this crossing.

blocks.title: Safety note
blocks.text: The application provides monitoring and warnings. Final safety decisions must follow local rules and responsible staff procedures.

polygon.lead: Polygon is the counting zone inside the camera image. Occupancy and waiting time are calculated when vehicles enter it.

blocks.title: Why polygon is needed
items: Even if the camera sees a wide area, the system counts only the needed road part.
When a vehicle enters the zone, Occupancy increases.
Long waiting inside the zone can produce yellow, orange or red warnings.

blocks.title: Color meanings
items: Green - zone is empty or no risk.
Yellow - vehicle is in the zone for a short time.
Orange - warning time threshold was exceeded.
Red - violation threshold was exceeded, or train is approaching while a vehicle is in the zone.

blocks.title: Good polygon rule
blocks.text: Do not make the zone too large. Mark only the road part related to the crossing. Too large gives false occupancy; too small can miss vehicles.

analytics.lead: Analytics page turns collected data into charts and official reports.

blocks.title: What you can see
items: Today's light/heavy vehicle distribution.
Hourly, weekly, monthly and yearly traffic statistics.
Train counts, passage times and durations.
Heatmap for busiest hours and days.

blocks.title: Export Word report
items: Open Analytics from the top toolbar.
Select the needed crossing on the left.
Click Download report.
Choose Today, 7 days, 30 days, 1 year or custom dates.
Click Download (.docx) and choose where to save the file.

blocks.title: Recommendation for official work
blocks.text: At the end of each month, save a 30-day report and export crossing settings as JSON backup.

troubleshooting.lead: Use these checklists to quickly separate the most common operator issues.

blocks.title: Camera is not visible
items: Check RTSP URL, login and password.
Check that PC and camera are on the same network.
Test RTSP URL in VLC.
Click Refresh or disable/enable the camera.

blocks.title: Vehicles are not counted
items: Check that detection is enabled.
Wait until AI model is loaded.
Check that polygon is not too small or in the wrong place.
Check that camera image is not too dark, blurry or badly angled.

blocks.title: PLC does not connect
items: Check PLC IP and port.
Check network cable and switch.
Make sure PLC is not locked by another program.
If no connection continues, call IT or automation specialist.

blocks.title: Report is not exported
items: Check that selected date range has data.
Check write permission for the target folder.
Close the Word file if it is already open, then export again.

version.lead: RailSafe AI is a local desktop product for railway crossing monitoring.

blocks.title: What's new (1.1.0)
items: ANPR — license plate recognition during train passage (separate thread, no real-time impact)
Automatic installer (install.bat) — detects GPU/CPU
Automatic CPU mode when no NVIDIA GPU
Word/PDF reports in three languages (uz/ru/en)
Improved stability and reliability

blocks.title: Minimum requirements
items: Windows 10 or Windows 11, 64-bit.
Intel Core i5 8th gen or AMD Ryzen 5 and newer.
At least 8 GB RAM, 16 GB recommended.
NVIDIA GPU makes AI faster; CPU mode may work without GPU.
Cameras must be available by RTSP.
PLC and cameras must be on the same local network as the computer.
